facts.claim: 作者提出笑话的“两个故事”模型：你以为在被讲的那个，和实际在讲的那个
facts.quote: One way of thinking about a joke is as two stories: the one you think you’re being told, and the one you’re actually being told.

facts.claim: 作者拆解“走进酒吧”类笑话：听众期待的酒吧其实是根长条金属，故事二由此揭开
facts.quote: it wasn’t the kind of bar you drink at, it was a long metal thing.

facts.claim: 作者用敲门笑话里的 Police 说明同一机制：名字被揭穿成另一句话
facts.quote: It wasn’t ‘Police’, the crime-fighters, it was ‘Police let me in, I need a poo’: an entirely different tale.

facts.claim: 作者分析 Groucho Marx 的双行笑话：第二行把第一行的场景整个推翻
facts.quote: One morning I shot an elephant in my pyjamas. How he got into my pyjamas, I’ll never know

facts.claim: 作者限定该模型并非万能，但断言多数笑话仍靠意外转折或揭露成立
facts.quote: Not all do this – sometimes the idea is just to make a point or seem really cool – but most jokes hinge on an unexpected turn or revelation.

facts.claim: 作者声明本书所收笑话大多依赖双关或同音词
facts.quote: But most of the jokes in this book involve some kind of wordplay.

facts.claim: 作者指出笑话也能被用于恶意：群体内部的黏合可反过来用来排挤外人
facts.quote: The way jokes can strengthen a group can also be used to make it clear to other people that they aren’t part of that group.

facts.claim: 作者以鲸鱼称重（weigh/whale）的双关突然收尾，把话题从严肃拽回烂笑话
facts.quote: Talking of weighty, where do you weigh a whale? At a whale weigh station.

relations.relation: 作者用“你以为在被讲的故事”这种第二人称框架，直接把读者拉进拆解过程。
relations.quote: A lot of great one- and two-line jokes are pretty much a setup followed by the revelation that what you thought was going on wasn’t going on at all.

relations.relation: 作者为全书选材划界：主体是双关型烂笑话，而非所有类型。
relations.quote: But most of the jokes in this book involve some kind of wordplay.

relations.pair: 作者 / 恶意用笑话的人
relations.relation: 作者把以笑话伤人定性为对正面事物的滥用，并以止咳糖浆砸眼睛作比。
relations.quote: This is a horrible misuse of a positive thing, like throwing a bottle of cough medicine at someone’s eye.

relations.relation: 作者承认“为何有人要用笑话作恶”值得更厚重的书，随即用一句双关把自己拉回轻佻。
relations.quote: Why anyone would choose to use jokes like that when they can use them to bring joy is a subject for a weightier and less fun book than this.

numbers.meaning: 作者把每个笑话拆成两层故事（误认的与真实的）
numbers.quote: One way of thinking about a joke is as two stories: the one you think you’re being told, and the one you’re actually being told.

numbers.meaning: 作者称大量优秀笑话只有一到两行，结构即“铺垫 + 反转”
numbers.quote: A lot of great one- and two-line jokes are pretty much a setup followed by the revelation that what you thought was going on wasn’t going on at all.

numbers.meaning: 德式香肠笑话里，“Nein”被反转成“八到十根”的数量
numbers.quote: and they said, ‘Nein’, then clarified that they’d eaten between eight and ten sausages.
